title: Budget Internalization: Fixed-Budget RLVR Trades Test-Time Scaling for In-Budget Accuracy
authors: Ilia Zavidnyi, Alexander Kovrigin, Arina Puchkova, Kirill Gelvan, Sergey Titov
date: 19 November 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version as of 23 November 2026)

code.title: JetBrains-Research/budget-internalization (Hugging Face collection)
code.label: checkpoints (Hugging Face)
code.note: Every trained checkpoint, ablations included, released with the paper under the base models' licences (78 model repositories on 23 November 2026). No training or evaluation code and no per-problem scores are released; the runs used the public NeMo RL framework and Inspect AI

takeaway: On three small models (Qwen3.5-4B, Gemma4-E2B, Nemotron-3-Nano-4B) trained with GRPO on math under a fixed rollout cap (three seeds for the main comparison), AIME accuracy at the cap rose 10.9 to 42.4 points over the base model while accuracy at the largest budget tested fell 13.1 to 30.2 points below it, and none of the tested fixes (single runs on Qwen3.5-4B) kept both the in-budget gain and the base model's test-time scaling.
takeaway_note: Seed means from the paper's Table 8. The introduction prints 11.7 to 46.7 and 17.2 to 35.0 for the same six checkpoints; its tables do not reproduce those ranges.
verdict: Believe the crossover: it appears in all 18 seeded runs on three model families, the tables reproduce every section 2 number, and the collapse in output length (27.3k to 5.0k tokens for Qwen) explains it. Treat the ranking of the fixes as suggestive: each is one run on one model, most of their 64k differences sit inside the printed 95% intervals and the 5-point spread between seeds, two levers of the objective were never varied, and the introduction's headline ranges do not match the paper's own tables.
